chunk_findings.detail: The new `target_of` probes the filesystem directly with `(Path(repo) / rel).is_file()` instead of going through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, violating [r-adapters] (“filesystem layout” must use an adapter so tests and swaps touch one place). chunk_findings.detail: When an existing CRLF file lacks a region and `force` is true, `_appended` builds each region with `render_region(doc, n, bodies[n])`; that embeds the `body-sha256` of the LF body from `rendered`, and only afterwards converts LF to CRLF in the whole block with `.replace("\n", eol)`. The appended region's body bytes in the file are then CRLF while its `body-sha256` marker hashes the LF body. Example: a CRLF `SECURITY.md` without the managed block, when exported with `--force`, gets a block whose body hash does not match its body. The next non-force refresh sees that mismatch as a hand-edited region and refuses to update it (or reports drift), so the file does not stabilize after the operator confirms the append.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/regions.py:_appended

chunk_findings.detail: The known-issues section ends with “Dependency advisories and security-pass findings are not recorded there, so they are not covered here.” This contradicts the stated intent that the known issues must include “findings of the security pass,” and the requirement that a version carrying an unfixed dependency advisory be marked vulnerable. Given a security-pass finding, the generated SECURITY.md will either omit it while falsely claiming it is not covered, or list it while the text says it is not, making the exported security policy inaccurate. chunk_findings.detail: `collect()` passes every security-tagged non-invalid bug to `_vulnerable()`, but `_vulnerable()` treats any bug without a `_Fix` as unfixed. A bug resolved `duplicate` (or `wontfix`, `notabug`) is not in `fixes` and `b.open` is false, so it is intentionally absent from the open/fixed known-issue lists, yet `_vulnerable()` still emits `vulnerable: <id>, not fixed yet` for the newest release. Concrete input: SEC-10 is tagged `security`, closed as duplicate of fixed bug SEC-0, and has no fix task. The SECURITY.md will permanently mark all current releases vulnerable to SEC-10, even though SEC-10 is a closed duplicate and SEC-0 is fixed. `_vulnerable()` should ignore non-open bugs that are not in `fixes`, matching the known-issues scope of open and fixed bugs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_security.py:_vulnerable

chunk_findings.detail: The new helper’s docstring promises “a blank line before each” appended missing region, but it builds `block` with `"\n".join(render_region(...) for n in names)`, which inserts only a single newline between consecutive region blocks. Since `render_region` returns a region ending at the end marker without a trailing newline (a newline after `-->` would be outside the region), using `force` to append more than one missing region produces adjacent end/start markers with no blank line, e.g. `<!-- ...:supported:end -->\n<!-- ...:known:start -->`. The exported SECURITY.md therefore loses the blank-line separation present in the template and can render its supported/known-issue sections incorrectly.

chunk_findings.detail: The template says "Dependency advisories and security-pass findings are not recorded there, so they are not covered here," and the matching help text in ddflow/templates/prompts/help/export.md describes Known Issues as only "bugs tagged `security` or `secbug`." This contradicts the change's own intent: dependency advisories are required to be shown in the Supported Versions table as "vulnerable: <id>, fixed in <ver>", and Known Issues must include "findings of the security pass." Given a dependency advisory or a security-pass finding, the exported SECURITY.md tells readers the item is not covered (or is omitted if the backend follows this text), so the required security disclosure is missing.

chunk_findings.detail: The implementation of `_is_security` checks `bool(wanted & set(b.tags)) or (item is not None and bool(wanted & set(item.tags)))`. However, `b.tags` and `item.tags` are expected to be collections of strings, but if either `b.tags` or `item.tags` is `None` or not an iterable of strings (for instance, if `Item.tags` can be `None` or another type based on the core model), `set(b.tags)` or `set(item.tags)` will raise a `TypeError` when `collect(q)` is executed. Given the core model fields for bugs and items, `tags` might be `None`, leading to a crash on export execution.

chunk_findings.detail: `collect()` passes every security-tagged non-invalid bug to `_vulnerable()`, but `_vulnerable()` treats any bug without a `_Fix` as unfixed. A bug resolved `duplicate` (or `wontfix`, `notabug`) is not in `fixes` and `b.open` is false, so it is intentionally absent from the open/fixed known-issue lists, yet `_vulnerable()` still emits `vulnerable: <id>, not fixed yet` for the newest release. Concrete input: SEC-10 is tagged `security`, closed as duplicate of fixed bug SEC-0, and has no fix task. The SECURITY.md will permanently mark all current releases vulnerable to SEC-10, even though SEC-10 is a closed duplicate and SEC-0 is fixed. `_vulnerable()` should ignore non-open bugs that are not in `fixes`, matching the known-issues scope of open and fixed bugs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_security.py:_vulnerable

chunk_findings.detail: The new helper queries the filesystem directly with `os.path.isfile(Path(repo) / rel)` instead of going through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, contrary to [r-adapters]. This is a new external dependency in `ddflow/services/export/ops.py`—e.g. every `target_of(repo, spec)` call performs ad-hoc filesystem-layout access that cannot be swapped or faked through the adapter layer.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/ops.py:target_of

chunk_findings.detail: The new helper’s docstring promises “a blank line before each” appended missing region, but it builds `block` with `"\n".join(render_region(...) for n in names)`, which inserts only a single newline between consecutive region blocks. Since `render_region` returns a region ending at the end marker without a trailing newline (a newline after `-->` would be outside the region), using `force` to append more than one missing region produces adjacent end/start markers with no blank line, e.g. `<!-- ...:supported:end -->\n<!-- ...:known:start -->`. The exported SECURITY.md therefore loses the blank-line separation present in the template and can render its supported/known-issue sections incorrectly.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/regions.py: _appended

chunk_findings.detail: The template says "Dependency advisories and security-pass findings are not recorded there, so they are not covered here," and the matching help text in ddflow/templates/prompts/help/export.md describes Known Issues as only "bugs tagged `security` or `secbug`." This contradicts the change's own intent: dependency advisories are required to be shown in the Supported Versions table as "vulnerable: <id>, fixed in <ver>", and Known Issues must include "findings of the security pass." Given a dependency advisory or a security-pass finding, the exported SECURITY.md tells readers the item is not covered (or is omitted if the backend follows this text), so the required security disclosure is missing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/export/security.md.j2:48-49

chunk_findings.detail: This new test file violates [r-adapters]: the helper `git()` calls `subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], ...)` directly, and later tests also manipulate the filesystem with `Path`/`os` instead of using the project’s adapter ports. The rule explicitly lists `git`, `subprocess tools`, and `filesystem layout` as external dependencies that must go through a port in `ddflow/adapters`, with tests using fakes rather than real subprocesses. Any environment without `git` on `PATH` makes every fixture in this file fail with `FileNotFoundError`, and the tests are not isolated behind a swappable fake as required.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_security.py:git

chunk_findings.detail: The implementation of `_is_security` checks `bool(wanted & set(b.tags)) or (item is not None and bool(wanted & set(item.tags)))`. However, `b.tags` and `item.tags` are expected to be collections of strings, but if either `b.tags` or `item.tags` is `None` or not an iterable of strings (for instance, if `Item.tags` can be `None` or another type based on the core model), `set(b.tags)` or `set(item.tags)` will raise a `TypeError` when `collect(q)` is executed. Given the core model fields for bugs and items, `tags` might be `None`, leading to a crash on export execution.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/export/kind_security.py:73

chunk_findings.detail: The new `none_here = len(sp.missing) == len(bodies)` is also true when `bodies` is empty — i.e. a bare-document export with no managed regions, a case the function already supports via its `bare_doc` parameter. For an existing bare-document target, `sp.missing` is empty, so `len(sp.missing) == len(bodies)` is `0 == 0`; without `--force` this sets `refuse` (“... has no ddflow region ...”) and `W._finish` refuses the write even though nothing was edited and no regions were missing. An input such as an existing `bare_doc=True` spec whose template renders no managed blocks now refuses every refresh without force, whereas the previous code did not. The condition should skip this refusal when `not bodies` (or otherwise exempt bare docs).
